author: Newsweek
title: Tennessee Gubernatorial Primary Tightens, With Marsha Blackburn Still Holding Lead Despite Aggressive Campaign by John Rose
text:
The race between U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn and U.S. Representative John Rose for the Tennessee governorship has become more competitive, with a final survey suggesting that Rose has narrowed the gap after an aggressive late campaign fueled by millions of dollars in self-financing. However, Blackburn remains the candidate to beat, with most public surveys continuing to show her holding a consistent advantage.
As Tennessee Republican s gear up to choose their nominee for governor, the race between U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn and U.S. Representative John Rose has seemingly become more competitive than many observers expected, according to one poll.
While Blackburn entered the contest as the overwhelming favorite, a final survey suggests Rose has narrowed the gap after an aggressive late campaign fueled by millions of dollars in self-financing, local outlets report. The primary has also been jolted recently following local reporting that Blackburn's Senate office was the subject of a confidential Senate Ethics Committee review into the alleged use of taxpayer-funded resources for political campaign activities.
While Blackburn's office says the matter was resolved and has denied wrongdoing, the investigation has become a point of attack in the gubernatorial primary, raising questions over transparency and ethics. Even so, Blackburn remains the candidate to beat, with most public surveys continuing to show her holding a consistent advantage. Midterm elections are commonly seen as a measure of public approval for the current president, and the president's party has traditionally lost seats during them.
There are currently 26 Republican governors nationwide compared to 24 Democratic-led states. In the 2024 presidential election, President Donald Trump overwhelmingly won Tennessee, by nearly 30 percent, versus then-Vice President Kamala Harris. Newsweek reached out to both Blackburn and Rose's campaigns via email on Wednesday night for comment
